# Native VoiceScribe migration

The prepared native bundle's `install.sh` handles the released VoiceScribe identity migration without running or installing Python. It moves owned data/configuration roots, rebases only managed retained-audio fields in SQLite history and the saved draft, and preserves unrelated text, external paths, model/audio/screenshot/editor stores, human titles and revisions. It migrates credential references, existing autostart state, Hyprland commands, recording overlays, plugin links, GNOME favorites/shortcuts and the same-user input-service template. It does not enable a new permission or merge conflicting state roots.

Migration and application installation share one transaction. A private persistent backup records original files, modes, links and desktop preferences; staged SQLite copies include committed WAL frames. Process failure or HUP/INT/TERM restores the original installation and user state. The retained backup container stays private. A service rename uses no-clobber semantics and retains the original inode identity so cancellation immediately after the move can still undo it. A competing service template is preserved. These checks establish process-failure recovery, not power-loss recovery or immunity to adversarial filesystem races.

## Independent reference

The immutable reference is v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. Unmodified released `linux/install.sh` invokes its actual `migrate_legacy.py`, SHA-256 `74e61565b12b914ba6a16e71c2304f1e4d51ba64e5fe54dd3b0e418b867a8445`. [The frozen output](released-legacy.json), SHA-256 `743a26ce72da4a28413ab13eb88e32a7e61ee00f8f08cbaf067fe78f36f7c900`, records 34 real released transactions. The temporary Python observer is confined to ignored `tmp/export-legacy.py`; it is not maintained or shipped.

Cases cover ordinary/Unicode/WAL/live/custom-XDG/custom-profile upgrades; dependency, desktop-cache and GNOME failures; data/configuration conflicts; foreign commands, extensions, autostart entries and plugin links; malformed or linked SQLite/JSON state; credential-profile conflicts; and enabled/disabled, failed, modified, conflicting or other-user services. External peers supply dependency provisioning, settings and service endpoints only. They do not implement migration, ownership, backups or rollback. Service peer writes require a verified disposable system-unit mount and never invoke host sudo or systemd.

The comparison observes process status, public output, requested integration operations, final preferences/service state and complete selected user/foreign/unit trees. It compares files by bytes/modes/links and SQLite by schema, columns, rows and integrity, using disposable database copies that cannot checkpoint the originals. Only temporary roots, UID, private backup names and the native no-clobber move options are normalized. Prepared Python/native application payloads and their public main launchers have a logical representation; actual native package integrity/execution is checked separately. Backup metadata JSON is compared structurally; WAL/SHM headers are represented by type/mode because their salts are process-specific. Additional before/after assertions require every backed-up file, including WAL/SHM, to retain its original bytes, mode and link target.

The initial observer hashed a linked foreign database containing a case-specific absolute path. Its corrected observation reads that database logically from a copy; the unchanged reference was recaptured. The first native successful upgrade reported a spurious recovery directory after moving its old application. Removing an unnecessary rewrite inside the retiring application fixed that failure. A real SIGTERM immediately after the service move then exposed duplicate old/new templates; the regression failed before the inode-based recovery repair. Those failures remain in `tmp/legacy-native-first.log` and `tmp/legacy-signal-before.log`.

The 34 comparisons and five native service interruption/ownership/recovery faults pass in `tmp/legacy-final.log` and `tmp/legacy-final-evidence/session.s0TpHC/`. The faults cover interruption during service startup, interruption immediately after its actual filesystem rename, competing destinations before the move or during rollback, and inability to stop the new service during recovery. They require the appropriate service state, restored preferences and original user bytes, absence of a completion marker and termination of the owned blocked descendant. Unsafe service recovery preserves its template and private backup with a bounded diagnostic. The failed-stop regression first failed on service state in `tmp/legacy-restore-owner-before.log`; rollback previously started the old service without confirming that the new one stopped. Absolute Python-trap positive controls prove that native transactions do not execute the interpreter. Recorded reference output remains under `tmp/legacy-reference-final-evidence/`.

## Scope and remaining gates

The actual nine-binary package is assembled and migrated in `tmp/legacy-package-evidence/session.kbW3xC/`, with results in `tmp/legacy-package.log`. Its real installer matches the complete portable legacy-state outcome, retains the original backup bytes, preserves the packaged inventory and starts from the public launcher with Python blocked. Modern installation/self-upgrade and the existing 19 reference outcomes, nine preservation cases, two interruption/ownership faults and six admission guards also pass. The migrated payload then passes the resident-process comparison (38 public states, 13 actions, five CLI contracts, second-instance forwarding, cold synthetic-PCM Record/quit and three startup faults). Public removal of its copied payload and all 39 released removal cases/six guards pass. Package, six remaining installer tests, resident and three uninstaller tests pass; the two migration tests were executed separately above.

All runs use synthetic contents and disposable prefixes inside private display/session/accessibility, network/PID/mount and device boundaries. No host input, microphone, clipboard, managed credential or real system-service change is exercised. Settings and privileged service effects are controlled external endpoints; this is not physical GNOME/Wayland or interactive sudo acceptance. Database compatibility is checked through real SQLite, not by claiming a visual History workflow.

The final workspace run, `tmp/legacy-workspace-final.log`, records 137 ordinary tests passed, zero failed and 57 environment checks ignored across 92 suites. The affected ignored checks were explicitly executed above. Strict workspace/all-target Clippy, formatting, diff checks and ShellCheck pass. Accepted session/accessibility logs contain no unexpected warning or critical. The final installed-app digest remains `1456c6af104ff95433b1d20ead793f628fada4ef9a67d76b5cf1dc4431885d67`, and the installed widget reports 1.6.0.

After building the production binaries, repeat the new migration comparisons through `dev/run-isolated-browser.sh` with `cargo test --locked -p mluva-install --test install native_legacy_ -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`. For the real payload, build it with the existing `package` test, set `MLUVA_TEST_NATIVE_BUNDLE` to `$OFFSCREEN_SESSION_ROOT/native-package/app` and execute `actual_native_bundle_migrates_legacy_state_and_starts`. The resulting installed path is recorded at `$OFFSCREEN_SESSION_ROOT/legacy-actual/installed-bundle` for the resident/removal comparisons.

The maintained root/source installer still belongs to the verified 1.6.0 release. Final entry-point/archive/dependency/license review, joined platform/device/UX acceptance, same-machine performance measurements and maintained/shipped Python removal remain required. All whole-workflow matrix rows stay Pending, and Daniel's installed app/widget remain 1.6.0. This milestone changes the draft task branch and disposable prefixes only.
